sections.sourcing: Q3 commentary flagged global supply-chain disruption — Middle East shipping issues delayed goods, squeezed air-freight capacity and pushed some Q4 deliveries forward — alongside European warehouse consolidation, including closing a Belgian DC serving Southern Europe. Higher year-on-year freight costs were the main external drag on Q3. Bangladesh remains the largest single sourcing base (~188 factories on the latest list), with LDC graduation in November 2026 adding duty exposure outside the EU (EU grace period runs to 2029).
sections.strategy: Q3 FY2026 (Jun–Aug, reported 24 Sept): operating profit up 23% to SEK 6.04bn, margin 10.6% vs 8.6%, on net sales of SEK 57.2bn (+1% in local currencies) with ~2% fewer stores. Gross margin reached 54.0%, but ~1.6pp came from one-off tariff/import effects that won't recur. CEO Daniel Ervér cited purchasing gains, cost control and a new simplified organisation, and said H&M is 'gradually increasing the proportion of in-season purchasing'.
sections.pricing: H&M expects somewhat higher Q4 markdowns than last year, citing Cyber Monday falling in November, inventory timing tied to supply-chain delays, and freight costs. September sales are guided +1% in local currencies. The shares fell despite the profit beat as investors focused on stalled growth.
sections.launches: Elie Saab x H&M confirmed: a 54-piece womenswear, menswear, accessories and footwear collection launching 22 October in selected stores and online, priced roughly $39.99–$429. Kelly Wearstler x H&M (29-piece interiors plus an 8-piece fashion capsule) has been live since 3 September, and the H&M Studio AW26 collection launched 24 September.
sections.gossip: Analysts called the quarter 'good if not spectacular'. The margin beat was widely read as cost- and tariff-driven rather than demand-driven, with Western Europe still weak. The UK head-office consultation (up to ~250 roles) is still being discussed in trade press.
soWhat: More in-season buying plus freight and Middle East disruption favour near-market and fast-turn capacity (Turkey, and Bangladesh/India vendors that can fly or split shipments). Pitch short lead times and small-batch flexibility.
Higher Q4 markdowns and the fading tariff one-off mean H&M will lean on buying margin into SS27, so expect firm FOB pressure and cautious bulk volumes.

The Elie Saab capsule (22 Oct) signals demand for embellished, occasionwear and tailoring fabrics. Suppliers of sequins, satins and suiting should target the next designer-collab and holiday-party programmes.
